    📅 09 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (762 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech 📈 Bullish 🌐 Thejournal ↗ Open Full Page

    Enterprise AI Spending Outpaces Adoption Growth, Report Finds

    📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (762 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Enterprise AI spending is growing faster than the number of organizations paying for it, according to a new Menlo Ventures report that points to a shift from buying access for employees to financing work performed by agents.
    • The venture capital firm's 2026 State of Enterprise AI report estimates deployment spending reached a $176.8 billion annualized run rate by September, up from $33 billion in 2025.
    • A larger bill can reflect broader use inside an organization, but it does not independently establish that the additional work is useful or profitable.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Enterprise AI spending is growing faster than the number of organizations paying for it, according to a new Menlo Ventures report that points to a shift from buying access for employees to financing work performed by agents.

    The venture capital firm's 2026 State of Enterprise AI report estimates deployment spending reached a $176.8 billion annualized run rate by September, up from $33 billion in 2025. The share of enterprises paying for AI rose from 55% to 65%.

    A larger bill can reflect broader use inside an organization, but it does not independently establish that the additional work is useful or profitable.

    Menlo's methodology describes revenue figures as annualized run rates. The $176.8 billion estimate therefore should not be read as $176.8 billion already spent during the first nine months of 2026.

    It has been revealed that the report also distinguishes unusually heavy spenders from the typical respondent. Average reported spending reached 4.7 times the prior year's level, while the median reached 2.2 times. That gap suggests a smaller group of large spenders drove the average substantially.

    Recent findings suggest that the practical implication is that an industry growth figure may be a poor benchmark for an individual organization's budget. Buyers need to understand their own workload growth and the results it produces.

    "Agents are changing the economics of software," Menlo principal Derek Xiao said in the firm's announcement.

    Menlo reports that agents account for 80% of tokens on OpenRouter, a service providing access to multiple models. That measures activity on one platform, rather than all enterprise AI use. Token consumption also measures processing volume, rather than completed business outcomes.

    An agent that makes repeated attempts can consume more resources without delivering proportionately more value. For procurement teams, the relevant comparison is consequently the cost of completing acceptable work, including the review it requires.

    It has been revealed that menlo estimates that Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google capture 69% of enterprise AI deployment spending. That measure is distinct from their shares of enterprise language-model API spending, a narrower category. The figures should not be used interchangeably.

    Sources indicate that the report draws on a Morning Consult survey of nearly 400 U.S. enterprise decision-makers responsible for more than $4 billion in AI spending. Market totals are modeled estimates informed by surveys, public filings, and third-party reports. Menlo discloses investments in Anthropic and OpenRouter.

    A separate announcement from Information Services Group describes buyers putting more emphasis on the economics and reliability of production deployments. ISG says ongoing security and observability work remains necessary as organizations scale.

    That provides a useful distinction between market demand and business value. Suppliers can generate growing revenue while customers still determine which deployments justify the cost.

    According to recent reports, for enterprise leaders, the newly introduced spending estimate strengthens the case for examining usage beyond license counts. It leaves the harder purchasing question with the customer: How much worthwhile work did the increased spending actually buy?

    Phishing Threats Totaled 7.3 Billion in Q3 2026

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • E-mail phishing threats reached 7.3 billion in Q3 2026, with September activity increasing 41% from August, according to Microsoft Threat Intelligence.
    • According to a report from Microsoft Threat Intelligence and the Microsoft Defender Security Research Team, phishing detections reached nearly 3 billion in September alone.
    • The findings also highlighted changes in attacker techniques, including business-service impersonation, credential theft, and social engineering through Microsoft Teams.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    E-mail phishing threats reached 7.3 billion in Q3 2026, with September activity increasing 41% from August, according to Microsoft Threat Intelligence.

    According to a report from Microsoft Threat Intelligence and the Microsoft Defender Security Research Team, phishing detections reached nearly 3 billion in September alone.

    The findings also highlighted changes in attacker techniques, including business-service impersonation, credential theft, and social engineering through Microsoft Teams.

    The Redmond-based firm recognized approximately 129 million malicious messages spoofing the sender domains of tracked business services during Q3.

    DocuSign was the most frequently spoofed brand in September, accounting for 29% of the month's tracked spoofing activity. Adobe, SurveyMonkey, and Barracuda also experienced increases toward the end of the quarter.

    The research found that some malicious messages were delivered despite failing e-mail authentication checks and being identified as threats.

    In September, tenant- or user-level security overrides applied to 63% of these messages with a recorded security outcome — most involved tenant-level exceptions.

    Microsoft warned that overly broad exceptions intended to support legitimate business communications can weaken protection against impersonation attacks.

    The firm emphasized that these findings do not establish whether recipients opened the messages or whether accounts were compromised.

    Microsoft also recorded approximately 141,000 malicious Teams call attempts during Q3.

    Attackers increasingly used ordinary personal names instead of explicitly impersonating IT support personnel. Such display names accounted for 46% of an observed sample in July, rising to 88% in September.

    Meanwhile, QR code phishing declined 67% compared to Q2, totaling roughly 12.1 million attacks.

    CAPTCHA-gated phishing activity increased toward the end of the quarter, reaching 3.1 million detected attacks in September. SVG attachments played a significant role in the increase.

    Credential theft remained the primary objective of malicious attachment campaigns, with approximately 94% to 96% of payload-based attacks directing users to phishing sites or fraudulent sign-in pages.

    Microsoft recommended reviewing Exchange Online Protection and Defender for Office 365 configurations, enabling Safe Links and Safe Attachments, and strengthening authentication protections.

    The company also advised organizations to review security exceptions and verify the identities of external Teams contacts before responding to suspicious requests.

    For more information, go to the Microsoft blog post.

    #31437. Anna Sui on the Five Films That Inspired Her Aesthetic

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (578 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Harpersbazaar ↗ Open Full Page

    Anna Sui on the Five Films That Inspired Her Aesthetic

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (578 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that here at Bazaar, we are just as devoted to the well-dressed mind as we are to the well-dressed woman.
    • In a recent development, anna Sui’s namesake brand is rooted in a reverence for the past.
    • Last week, the Friends of the Costume Institute, an organization attached to the Met museum, asked Sui to dive into her vast collection of archival references and select a film that most influenced her as a designer for a screening.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that here at Bazaar, we are just as devoted to the well-dressed mind as we are to the well-dressed woman. In fact, we find that one often engenders the other. In our new series The Well-Dressed Mind, we examine the intersection point between style and intellect by asking industry professionals and tastemakers for their cultural recommendations.

    In a recent development, anna Sui’s namesake brand is rooted in a reverence for the past. By blending niche references across time periods, she makes her clothes feel distinctly now. Part of a defining generation of downtown Upcoming York designers in the ’80s and ’90s, Sui invokes her love of vintage fashion, design, photography, and art as the basis of her work. The feel of the resulting collections is at once girlish, grunge, ’70s, punk, and bohemian.

    Last week, the Friends of the Costume Institute, an organization attached to the Met museum, asked Sui to dive into her vast collection of archival references and select a film that most influenced her as a designer for a screening. (Sui also funds a yearlong internship for the department.) She picked the 1970 movie Performance, directed by Donald Cammell and Nicolas Roeg, which depicts a London gangster’s identity crisis while in hiding at the home of a rock star (played by Mick Jagger) and his two girlfriends, one of whom is played by style icon Anita Pallenberg. You can see why this would appeal to her; the trippy, ’70s clash of glam and bohemia is very Sui.

    Hungry for more, we asked Sui to outline the onus behind that selection and four additional films that had the greatest influence on her aesthetic.

    Directed by Donald Cammell and Nicolas Roeg.

    “Anita Pallenberg has always been my style icon, especially since I saw her amazing wardrobe throughout Performance: the fringe kaftan, antique lace top, pink velvet pants, fox fur coat, silver platform sandals, texture zigzag tights, and the slinky black satin dresses.”.

    “This film is set in a brothel in 1930s fascist Italy. The lingerie, piano shawls with smoky eye makeup and wavy bobs looked straight out of a Sarah Moon photograph.”.

    “Jane Birkin is a fashion model with a Peeping Tom for a neighbor. He’s obsessed with what he perceives as her glamorous fashion lifestyle, and he comes to the rescue when she decides to do herself in. It’s got sets by the artistic collective the Fool, which designed the Beatles’ Apple Boutique, and a George Harrison soundtrack to transport you to the swinging ’60s in London.”.

    “The Who’s rock opera has a star-studded cast: Ann-Margret, Oliver Reed, Jack Nicholson, Elton John, Eric Clapton, Keith Moon, Tina Turner, and Roger Daltrey. There are amazing costumes by his wife, Shirley Russell, including Biba clothes on their daughter Victoria. This musical odyssey is filled with the amazing Who soundtrack.”.

    In a recent development, “Liza Minnelli's talent and effervescent personality brought to life the dynamo Sally Bowles. With an incredible cast—divinely decadent Joel Grey, gorgeous Michael York, and Marisa Berenson—we're transported to the Kit Kat Club and 1930s Weimar Republic Germany. The songs and music are just as sensational as Bob Fosse’s choreography and direction. And Liza’s costumes, with a helping hand from Halston, are legendary. She even wears an embellished Ossie Clark for one musical number. Her green nail polish, spiky false eyelashes, and signature haircut have stayed with me forever. One of the greatest musical dramas of all time.”.

    Sources indicate that every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

    Every season, there’s a latest breakthrough color. Last year, we saw butter yellow and tomato red take over, and this fall we’ve seen burgundy star as the hue of the season. Now, cobalt blue is taking center stage, and we’re here for it.

    Recent findings suggest that striking and statement-making, cobalt blue is one of our favorite standout color trends yet. It’s bold, yes, but somehow it can seamlessly transition from a star-of-the-show satin top or sparkling pump to a foundational cardigan or cashmere sweater. The color gained traction on last season’s runways, but it’s since permeated street-style culture around the world. One of our favorite ways to wear cobalt is with an eye-catching accessory, and Dior’s Mini Book Tote is currently topping our holiday wish lists.

    But even if you’re not in the market for a new handbag, there are plenty of ways to wear the shade. Whether you’re headed on a Sunday stroll through your local holiday market or hitting a fancy festive soirée, we’ve found a cobalt blue-inspired outfit that’s bringing a little colorful cheer to your winter ensemble.

    Make cobalt the main event with a brazen blue overcoat. Paired with patent heeled boots and sporty styling underneath, this is the perfect off-duty outfit—taking you from a workout to brunch. We’re also loving @designedbychep’s custom embroidered sweaters (which can come in cobalt threading!), and a lighter blue-hued bag for contrast.

    Italian Cashmere Triangle Scarf.

    @designedbychep Hand-Embroidered Knicks Sweatshirt.

    Splits59 River Airweight Stirrup Leggings.

    Jacquemus Valérie Top-Handle Bag.

    Nomasei ARIA - Ankle Boots - Patent Black.

    Flip the script and wear your cobalt as a layer underneath an oversize trench. ATM and Aligne both make great colorful basics, while Jenni Kayne’s quiet luxury takes form in a structured overcoat. The cobalt strap on Moon Boot’s fluffy ballerinas is a nice touch.

    Aligne Marianne Cord Wide Leg Trousers.

    Lié Studio The Caroline Earrings.

    Sources indicate that take the trend to your holiday party, pairing sleek satin with a luxe leather to elevate your look. A sparkly cobalt heel ties in the top, and Larroudé makes the perfect pair.

    Ryan Roche Silk Bias High-Neck Blouse.

    Larroudé by Sergio Hudson Addison Pumps.

    Ring Concierge Open Diamond Wrap Ring.

    David Yurman Crossover Three Row Huggie Hoop Earrings.

    Frame x Ritz Classic Trench Coat.

    White & Warren Cashmere Travel Wrap.

    According to recent reports, if you’re looking to test the cobalt blue waters, start with a radiant accessory. White & Warren’s vibrant travel wrap and Clare V’s more muted bags offer different levels of brazenness, so you can choose which feels more suited to you.

    Sources indicate that A casual, off-duty look takes a trend-forward turn with Guest in Residence’s cardigan. Paired with AG’s beloved lightly baggy jeans and polished with Scarosso’s easy loafers, running errands has never looked so chic.

    Dorothee Schumacher Fluffy Moment Coat.

    Guest in Residence Stealth Cardigan.

    Alexis Bittar Molten Gold Spiral Hoop Earrings.

    Christopher Esber Turnlock Suede Mini Bag.

    #31419. Latest Update: A Kitchen in Bloom: How Tiffany Howell and Miele Reimagine the Heart of the Home

    Latest Update: A Kitchen in Bloom: How Tiffany Howell and Miele Reimagine the Heart of the Home

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (864 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elledecor

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that when Tiffany Howell of Night Palm Interiors designs a home, her vision transcends conventional norms, veering into an ethereal realm—an approach she calls “the poetry of place.” In Howell’s mind, film, fashion, and music are as essential as decorative art, and she uses these inspirations to create theatrical spaces that ignite all the senses—layering texture, sound, scent, light, and form to evoke deep emotion.
    • Sources indicate that when Miele partnered with Howell to create a dream kitchen for an installation at Art Basel, she seized the opportunity to reimagine what a kitchen can be.
    • According to recent reports, “I do think the kitchen is really one of the most tender rooms in the house,” Howell notes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that when Tiffany Howell of Night Palm Interiors designs a home, her vision transcends conventional norms, veering into an ethereal realm—an approach she calls “the poetry of place.” In Howell’s mind, film, fashion, and music are as essential as decorative art, and she uses these inspirations to create theatrical spaces that ignite all the senses—layering texture, sound, scent, light, and form to evoke deep emotion. When executed with this level of intention, a room becomes an environment you don't merely look at but fundamentally feel.

    Sources indicate that when Miele partnered with Howell to create a dream kitchen for an installation at Art Basel, she seized the opportunity to reimagine what a kitchen can be. The result is the interactive 360-degree rendering seen here—a wildly imaginative digital environment that inspired the brand’s upcoming physical installation at Miami’s premier art fair. “I wanted an undeniable sexiness, a beautiful, sensory experience,” she says. “I created the space with characters in mind that I’d invite to a dinner party in this kitchen.” After all, the kitchen is a home’s heartbeat, an interactive space with multiple purposes.

    According to recent reports, “I do think the kitchen is really one of the most tender rooms in the house,” Howell notes. She leaned into that romance by installing black cabinetry with blossoming branches and birds in iridescent greens and pinks. The cabinets are an homage to her love of 1920s chinoiserie furniture and fashion, seen through a very glamorous, Los Angeles lens. That California focus also meant bringing the outdoors in. The grand conservatory space harnesses diffused, natural light with the promise of the scent of jasmine wafting into the room. Howell’s ideal playlist sets the tone with jazz greats and ambient synth-pop.

    “I wanted to create a kitchen that’s a completely sensory experience,” Howell explains. “The sound of a crackling warm fireplace, the aroma of a meal cooked for loved ones, or of making coffee in the morning.” For Howell, these aren't incidental details; they are the sensory architecture that turns raw space into lived emotion. In Howell’s view, this kitchen is “also a place where you can take a nap, read a book, or write in your journal. Every moment in this room can become a ritualistic experience of living well.”.

    When it came to the practical needs of a kitchen, Howell used Miele as a muse, an invitation to eschew the pale minimalism so common in luxury kitchens. “The appliances are so elegant, they kind of act as the jewelry of the room,” she notes. “And their functionality and ease of operation give you back time to live better, relax with a drink, hang out with family and friends, and create the stories that make up a life.”.

    Consider the Miele Built-In Coffee System and wine cooler in matching dark finishes which are nearly camouflaged so the technology reads more as furniture than appliance. That tension between heirloom design and high-tech styling becomes a unified part of a lived-in, well-collected home. Accent pieces, including a vintage Fortuny pendant lamp over the kitchen island, and upholstered chairs in the conservatory with detailing reminiscent of antique lingerie, create a moody environment well suited to Miele's black-finished lines that resemble rich obsidian.

    It has been revealed that the 36” Full Surface Induction Cooktop features a frameless, flush design that disappears into a dark-veined countertop. Transforming the entire glass surface into one expansive cooking area, it fits up to six pots or pans at once and with Intelligent Pan Recognition and SmartSelect White controls seamlessly transfer power settings wherever pans are moved. On the same wall is the 30” Handleless Combi-Steam Oven XXL, with DualSteam technology that emanates ASMR sounds of steam cooking, and a black glass façade that resembles a framed panel or window. From the cool, flush glide of the induction cooktop to the whisper-quiet hum of precision steam, the technology engages the senses rather than interrupting them, turning modern convenience into an intuitive, tactile ritual. Rather than breaking up the wall with a stack of conspicuous appliances, these seamless integrations keep the architecture artful. And for added convenience, Miele’s elegant touch controls are enhanced with Wi-Fi connectivity for an easier user experience.

    Howell’s concealment of technology is exhibited in her use of the 42” French Door Refrigerator with its elongated custom handles and a dark lacquered paneled front that echoes the floral chinoiserie motifs—an unconventional solution that turns a mundane appliance into a piece of decorative art. Once the refrigerator doors are open, the Brilliant Light Pro illumination makes it easy to survey the food inside the large capacity interior.

    “How do you nurture yourself and others in the kitchen?” Howell asks. Her answer: a design that creates a restorative space evoking intimacy and slowness, where technology can encourage a lightness and give us back more time. By composing every sight, surface, scent, and sound into a single harmonious narrative, Howell proves that a kitchen shouldn't just be an aesthetic statement—it should be something you feel in your bones. “What excites me is building a new world with more possibilities,” Howell notes. “I don’t think I could design any other way.”.

    #31417. ‘He Needs To Be Layered’: Bond Girl Léa Seydoux Shares the Most Important Traits for the Next 007

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (397 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Elle ↗ Open Full Page

    ‘He Needs To Be Layered’: Bond Girl Léa Seydoux Shares the Most Important Traits for the Next 007

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (397 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Elle

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, if there’s one Bond girl who has influenced the course of 007 history more than anyone, it’s Dr.
    • Industry observers note that appearing in the last two films in the series—Spectre (2015) and No Time to Die (2021)—Dr.
    • Asked whether she would consider a return to the franchise, now under the creative direction of Amazon MGM Studios and without Daniel Craig as 007, the actor stated: “I really loved working with Barbara Broccoli and her brother Michael [G.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, if there’s one Bond girl who has influenced the course of 007 history more than anyone, it’s Dr. Madeleine Swann. Played by French actor Léa Seydoux, who is this month’s ELLE UK cover star, psychotherapist Dr. Swann disrupts the James Bond narrative in a way that no previous lover has done: She challenges his misogyny.

    Industry observers note that appearing in the last two films in the series—Spectre (2015) and No Time to Die (2021)—Dr. Swann has a long-term relationship with secret agent 007, eventually telling him that he’s the father of her daughter, making Seydoux’s part in the legendary franchise unique.

    Asked whether she would consider a return to the franchise, now under the creative direction of Amazon MGM Studios and without Daniel Craig as 007, the actor stated: “I really loved working with Barbara Broccoli and her brother Michael [G. Wilson]. It was one of the best experiences, a pure delight. And I don’t know, it will be different.”.

    She has already worked with Denis Villeneuve, the director attached to the next Bond film, in Dune: Part Two. “He’s a great choice, let’s see. I’m curious how they will reinvent it. But for me, it will never be the same because it was Barbara’s father who initiated the Bond movies. Now, I don’t know,” she told ELLE. “It became American….I hope they will keep the British spirit.”.

    As for casting Seydoux in the role, former Bond producer Barbara Broccoli noted that her scenes in No Time to Die still move her to tears. “When we were filming the goodbye scene at the Italian train station, Léa approached it with such subtlety—she grasped her stomach to express her pain, but also the secret heartbreak that she was carrying James’s child. It moved me to tears then and continues to move me each time I watch it.”.

    It has been revealed that as for the question of who will play Bond, she won’t be drawn into the speculation. (This was before Robert Pattinson was unveiled to take on the mantle on November 16.) Seydoux admits that finding the right person to replace Daniel Craig is difficult. “He needs to be layered, you know? And that is something that’s hard to find in young actors.”.

    Léa Seydoux appears next in Gentle Monster, which begins streaming on Netflix on November 18.
